description:
Carved out of JMAP-g7wu.2.4.2: handler-side permission enforcement.

Site: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/space.rs in handle_chat_space_set, after parsing the SpacePatchOp Vec but before calling backend.apply_space_patch().

Per draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §Space/set lines 1093, 1096, 1102, 1105, 1108, 1111, 1114, 1117, 1120, 1123, 1126, 1129:
- manage_space: addRoles/removeRoles/updateRoles space-wide metadata wired to update arm
- manage_roles: addRoles/removeRoles/updateRoles family
- manage_members: addMembers/removeMembers/updateMembers family
- manage_channels: addChannels/removeChannels/updateChannels + addCategories/removeCategories/updateCategories families

This bead requires:
1. New helper in chat-server: resolve_caller_permissions(backend, caller, account_id, space_id) -> HashSet<String> — reads the Space, finds the caller's memberships, unions their roles' permissions plus @everyone defaults.
2. Per-op variant -> required-permission mapping helper.
3. Reject the whole patch if the caller lacks any required permission (or partial-success: reject only the disallowed ops? The spec is ambiguous; recommend whole-patch reject to match RFC 8620 /set atomicity expectations for that update target).

Note: role-position-hierarchy enforcement (members may only add/modify roles whose 'position' is strictly less than their own highest-position role) is OUT OF SCOPE for this bead — that check is in JMAP-g7wu.2.4.3 because it must be atomic with the mutation (backend-side).

Deferred from .4.2 because the handler-permission-resolution helper is new infrastructure with its own design surface (where memberships live in Space, how @everyone defaults work, how chat-server consumers configure them) and is itself ~150-300 LOC + tests.
title: Handler-side permission gates for handle_chat_space_set (manage_space / manage_roles / manage_members / manage_channels)
